primitives.name: Robust Accuracy-Diversity trimming
primitives.verbatim_quote: This paper proposes the first algorithm addressing all three simultaneously (RAD) with a criterion (ADT) that trades off accuracy against diversity instead of pursuing either alone, plus five benchmark algorithms (None, R, A, D, AutoRAD) and practical guidelines for which to use.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S': 'set of forecasters', 'MSE_i': 'mean squared error of forecaster i (dimensionless)', 'MSEC_{i,j}': 'mean squared error difference between forecasters i and j (dimensionless)', '\\kappa': 'diversity-weight parameter (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Forecasters are independently evaluated on validation data; MSEC captures pairwise disagreement; ADT balances accuracy and diversity trade-off.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When RelDiv < 0.2, diversity is negligible; when RelDiv > 0.5, full RAD is required.

layer2.mapping: RAD's ADT criterion enables GSE to select optimal forecaster subsets by balancing predictive accuracy and ensemble diversity, reducing overfitting and improving generalization.
layer2.telemetry: Trimmed pool size, validation MSE, and MSEC across iterations

reasoning_traces.think:
The RAD algorithm operates by constructing a composite trimming criterion ADT that explicitly balances accuracy and diversity. It begins with a Tukey's-fences screen to remove unstable forecasters, then performs backward elimination using ADT to iteratively refine the pool. The key insight is that diversity, while beneficial, can degrade performance if misapplied—especially in isolation. The paper demonstrates that trimming for diversity alone (D) is consistently detrimental, whereas joint trimming (RAD) improves accuracy and robustness. The RelDiv diagnostic provides a principled way to determine whether diversity matters at all, guiding the choice between accuracy-only (A), diversity-only (D), or joint (RAD) strategies. The mathematical structure of ADT allows for dynamic adjustment of the trade-off parameter κ, enabling adaptive trimming. In GSE, this translates to a state transition system where the trimming strategy evolves based on empirical diagnostics. The failure mode occurs when diversity is pursued without considering accuracy, leading to inclusion of poor performers. Conversely, ignoring diversity risks overfitting to a narrow set of models. The algorithm's robustness stems from its reliance on validation-set metrics rather than training-set overfitting.
